diagnostic_evidence.quote: Pick $R\ge\magn M+n^2\rho$ so that $\Pr(\magn{M+N}\le R)\le e^{-n}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition a19's conclusion contains the additive term Pr(||M+N_g||_infty >= R). The proof of Theorem a1 bounds f(m,eps) = sup_{||M'||<=R} Pr(sigma_{n-m}(M'+N) <= eps) by applying a19 to each M', but this term is never controlled or carried: the proof's chains end at '<= 1/n^K + R^{20K} e^{-rho n}'. With the proof's spectral-norm-scale choice R >= ||M|| + n^2 rho the term is not small: for M' = M - zI with ||M||_infty >> ||M|| + n^2 rho (e.g. M = c 11^T, where ||M||_infty = cn^2 but ||M|| = cn), or for M' = 1.5R e_1 w* inside the sup over ||M'|| <= 1.5R+eps, the event ||M'+N||_infty >= R holds with probability approximately 1, so a19's bound is vacuous and the displayed inequalities in Theorem a1's proof are unjustified for such M.

failure_location.quote: Now we would like to apply Proposition \ref{a19} with $m=0$ and $m=1$ to bound $f(m,\eps)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a second parameter R_1 >= ||M||_infty + O(log n) (or Theta(nR)) for the infinity-norm truncation in Lemmas a18/a19 so that Pr(||M'+N||_infty >= R_1) <= e^{-n}, carry that term through, and recalibrate eta downward in Theorem a1; the stated exponents 10K and 35K have enough slack that the final statements survive.
issues.overall_effect: The bounds of Theorem a1 (and transitively the algorithmic theorem thm:added-1) are unproven, in every sparsity regime, for matrices whose infinity norm greatly exceeds their spectral norm; the claim in the technical overview that the singular-value bound holds 'with beta(n) = O(exp(-rho n))' is likewise unestablished.
issues.title: Theorem a1's proof drops the uncontrollable infinity-norm tail of Proposition a19
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained two-parameter re-derivation and recalibration (a reoptimization) with no new architecture and no loss of stated conclusions, but it is more than a constant tweak of the main proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Take it to be that upper bound divided by $R^{2K+2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding display bounds Pr(kappa(lambda_1)^2 >= 1/(n^2 eta^{2/3})). With the proof's choice eta^{2/3} = rho^{1+K}/(8 n^{4+K} R^{4K+2}), that threshold equals 8 n^{2+K} R^{4K+2}/rho^{1+K}, which is at least 8 n^{3+2K} R^{2K} (since R >= n^2 rho gives R^2 >= n rho). Hence the event {kappa^2 >= 8n^{3+2K}R^{2K}} is strictly larger than the event that was bounded, and the asserted bound at the smaller threshold does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the derived threshold 1/(n^2 eta^{2/3}) = 8 n^{2+K} R^{4K+2}/rho^{1+K} in place of 8n^{3+2K}R^{2K} and re-verify the final bounds, which the exponents' slack permits.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate display in Theorem a1's proof is unjustified; the final thresholds (||M||+n^2 rho)^{10K} and (||M||+n^2 rho)^{-35K} remain derivable once the correct threshold is used, because the stated exponents have slack.
issues.title: Invalid threshold substitution in the proof of Theorem a1
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction of the displayed threshold; the subsequent verification is routine and every stated claim of Theorem a1 survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note $\kappa_V(A)=\kappa_V((n/\delta)M+N)$ so Theorem \ref{a1} means with high probability that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies Theorem a1 to (n/delta)M + N, using kappa_V(A) = kappa_V((n/delta)M+N). Theorem a1's hypothesis for that matrix requires n rho = Omega(log n * log(n||M||/delta + n)), which contains an additive log(1/delta) term; thm:added-1 assumes only n rho = Omega(log n log(n+||M||)). For delta with log(1/delta) >> log(n+||M||) the invocation is outside Theorem a1's hypotheses, and the kappa_V control (which the proof itself states with a log(1/delta) term) is unestablished, so the (1+-eps) guarantee with the stated number k of iterations is unproven in that range.

failure_location.quote: For each $\rho$ satisfying $n\rho=\Omega(\log(n)\log(n+\magn M))$ and $\eps,\delta\in(0,1)$, there is an algorithm $\alg{specr}(A)$ which computes a value such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to n rho = Omega(log n (log(n+||M||) + log(1/delta))), matching Theorem a1 applied to (n/delta)M.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithmic guarantee of thm:added-1 is unestablished for high-precision delta at the stated sparsity; for extremely small delta no rho <= 1 can satisfy the hypothesis actually needed.
issues.title: thm:added-1's sparsity hypothesis omits the log(1/delta) needed to apply Theorem a1
issues.why_classification: A routine hypothesis addition repairs the proof, but it withdraws part of the advertised scope (all delta in (0,1) at fixed sparsity), which is a real, though limited, loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem \ref{a1} means with high probability that

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts the two-sided approximation unconditionally. The proof derives it only on events of probability 1 - O(n^{-K}) - 1/n: the shattering event from Theorem a1 ('with high probability'), the concentration event for ||A^k b||, and implicitly ||N|| <= n so that the added perturbation (delta/n)N has norm at most delta. Each fails with positive probability (e.g. the Gaussian-tail event ||N|| > n), and already for M = 0 the output can then exceed (1+eps)delta while specr(E) <= delta for every ||E|| <= delta, so the unconditional statement is false as written.

failure_location.quote: there is an algorithm $\alg{specr}(A)$ which computes a value such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'with probability at least 1 - O(n^{-K}) - 1/n' to the guarantee in the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee type of thm:added-1 is misstated: it is a high-probability guarantee, not a deterministic one.
issues.title: thm:added-1 states an unconditional guarantee but the proof only establishes it with high probability
issues.why_classification: The intended high-probability guarantee is exactly what the proof establishes; adding the standard qualifier preserves the method, rate, and scope.

issues.failure_explanation: On G and {||A|| <= R}, Proposition a11 applied to A/R together with (a27) gives max_j kappa(lambda_j)^2 <= n^2 4^n (R/eta_0)^{2n-2}. But the chosen K = ceil(n lg(3R/eta_0) + lg(eta_0/tau_0)) only yields tau_K >= tau_0 2^K >= eta_0 (3R/eta_0)^n, which is smaller than the needed bound by the factor n^2 (4/3)^n (R/eta_0)^{n-2}/eta_0 > 1 whenever eta_0 is at most n^2 (4/3)^n (in particular for all intended uses, where eta_0 is tiny). Hence G and ||A|| <= R does not imply F(tau_K), so step (a29), which conditions on this implication, is unjustified.

failure_location.quote: Then $\tau_K\ge \eta_0(3R/\eta_0)^n$ and so Lemma \ref{a11} combined with (\ref{a27}) implies $G\wedge\magn{A}\le R\implies F(\tau_K)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take K = ceil(2n lg(3R/eta_0) + lg(2/tau_0)), so that tau_K >= 2 (3R/eta_0)^{2n} >= n^2 4^n (R/eta_0)^{2n-2}, and replace the constant in a14's conclusion by approximately 6n lg(3R/eta_0) + 3 lg(2/tau_0).
issues.overall_effect: Proposition a14's stated conclusion, with constant 3n lg(3R/eta_0) + 3 lg(2 eta_0/tau_0), is not established; a version with a roughly doubled constant holds. Theorem a1's proof absorbs the change with room to spare.
issues.title: Proposition a14's bootstrap uses too few steps for the deterministic implication
issues.why_classification: A short local repair (redefining K) that changes only an absolute constant in the error term of a14; the method, conclusion, and all downstream results survive unchanged in substance.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\net$ be an $r$-net of the disk of radius $R$.

issues.failure_explanation: An r-net guarantees every point of the disk a net point within distance r. Given |lambda_i - lambda_j| = eta(A) <= r, a net point within r of the midpoint of the pair is only within r + eta/2 <= 1.5r of each eigenvalue, so there need not exist a net point within r of both (1D example: the net {-0.2, 1.7} has covering radius 1 on [0,2], yet no net point is within 1 of both 0 and 1). A net of radius r/2 is required; its size is at most about 4 pi (R/r)^2, and the stated bound |N| <= pi(R/r)^2 on the net size is itself optimistic by a constant factor for any standard net.

failure_location.quote: if they're both inside the disk, then there must be some $z\in\net$ such that $\lambda_i,\lambda_j\in\ball(z,r)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an (r/2)-net (or keep the r-net and track the 1.5r distortion), adjusting the constant in a21's conclusion accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a21's conclusion holds only with a constant factor (about 4 to 9) in place of pi in front of R^2/r^2; Theorem a1's proof absorbs this constant.
issues.title: Lemma a21's r-net covering claim is false
issues.why_classification: A routine local repair of the net radius changes only an absolute constant in the lemma's bound; the conclusion's form, the exponents, and all downstream uses survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We therefore obtain the overall bound of $\binom{n}{m+1}s^{m+1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of a19 must fix a parameter s in the interval [2^{3(K+1)} eps^2 n^2 R^{2K}/rho^K, rho/n] required by Lemma a18 (s is never quantified in a18's statement and never chosen in a19's proof), and Lemma a16 then contributes binom(n,m+1) s^{m+1} (a16's statement says binom(n,m), but its own proof derives binom(n,m+1)). Even at the minimal admissible s, this exceeds a19's first term n^{2+m+1} R^{2K(m+1)} eps^{2(m+1)} by at least 2^{3(K+1)}/rho^K >= 2^9 for m = 0, and for m = 1 by at least 2^{6(K+1)} n / rho^{2K} >> 1 in every regime; the factor is polynomial in n for rho = n^{alpha-1} and superpolynomial for rho of order log^2(n)/n. Hence the stated constant in a19 is not established by its proof.

failure_location.quote: We obtain the final result by a union bound.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose s explicitly at its minimum admissible value, correct a16's statement to binom(n,m+1), restate a19's first term as (up to constants) 2^{3(K+1)} n^{m+3} rho^{-K} R^{2K(m+1)} eps^{2(m+1)}, and recalibrate eta in Theorem a1 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition a19's quantitative bound is understated by a polynomial to superpolynomial factor; Theorem a1's proof, which cites this constant, must be recalibrated (this succeeds: the rho^{-K} factor cancels against rho^{1+K} in the choice of eta, and the exponents 10K and 35K have room), so the final statements survive.
issues.title: Proposition a19's constant is not derivable: s is never chosen and the a16/a18 union exceeds the stated term
issues.why_classification: The stated numerical bound of a central proposition must be weakened by a polynomial-to-superpolynomial factor and the main proof recalibrated, but the method, exponents, and the final theorems' conclusions all survive, yielding a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the last step follows from the hypotheses of this lemma

issues.failure_explanation: In the regime allowed by Theorem a1's hypothesis, e.g. n rho = Theta(log n log(||M||+n)) with ||M|| <= poly(n) (so K = Theta(log n / log log n) and R >= n^2 rho), Lemma a18's two conditions on the never-quantified parameter s are contradictory. The first, needed for the step to [(1-rho)^j + rho/2]^n, forces s >= 2^{3(K+1)} eps^2 n^2 R^{2K}/rho^K, hence log(s/(2 eps^2)) >= 2K log R + K log(1/rho) + 2 log n - O(K) = Theta((log n)^2 / log log n). The second requires log(s/(2 eps^2)) <= rho n^{K/(K+1)}/(2 log(2/s)^{1/(K+1)}) = Theta(log n). No admissible s exists, so a19's proof cannot be carried out at all in this regime (under any parsing of the second hypothesis). Moreover the union bound inside a18, with the paper's own net-size bound, requires log(es/(2 eps^2)) * (log(2/s)/rho)^{1/K} <= n rho; the forced lower bound on log(s/(2 eps^2)) together with log(2/s) >= log(2n/rho) makes the left side omega((log n)^2) = omega(n rho), so the net sizes overwhelm the probability decay by a diverging factor (the j = 1 case of estimate (a32) is also vacuous as written, giving max(1, 1/2)^n = 1). Consequently a19, and with it Theorem a1 and thm:added-1 whose hypotheses permit this regime, is not established for sparse perturbations, i.e. precisely the headline claim (a) of O(n log^2 n) perturbed entries. For polynomial sparsity n rho = n^{1-alpha} the hypotheses are compatible and the argument goes through modulo the other issues.

failure_location.quote: the event $\sigma_{n-m}(M+N_g)\le\eps$ is the union of the events whose probabilities are bounded in each of Lemma \ref{a16} and Lemma \ref{a18}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must re-derive the net argument of Lemma a18 with a scale-sensitive counting (charging the fine grid only to the a_k entries above the k-th threshold rather than to all a_{k+1} nonzero entries), replace the second hypothesis on s by a condition that is actually satisfiable when n rho = Theta(log n log(||M||+n)), fix the j = 1 boundary of estimate (a32), and re-verify the full calibration; failing that, Theorem a1 must be restricted to polynomial sparsity, excluding the advertised O(n log^2 n)-entry regime.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem a1 and thm:added-1 are unproven in the sparse regime n rho = Theta(log n log(||M||+n)) (down to rho of order log^2(n)/n), which is the paper's main advertised novelty over prior work; the abstract's claim (a) and the corresponding table row are unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma a18's hypotheses are unsatisfiable in the sparse regime, so a19 and Theorem a1 are unproven for rho ~ log^2(n)/n
issues.why_classification: The proof of the central proposition fails provably (contradictory hypotheses) in the headline sparse regime, and the only conceivable repairs either require essentially re-engineered net-counting arguments whose success is unverified or exclude the advertised O(n log^2 n)-entry regime; a speculative repair does not lower the severity.
